newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Kabul airport hit by rockets.
newsitem.headline: Kabul airport hit by rockets.

text.p: Several rockets landed within the perimeter of Kabul airport on Sunday, forcing military and civilian aircraft to scramble for safety but causing little apparent damage, witnesses said.

The barrage was apparently launched by forces of ousted government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood, who in the past few days has taken a military airbase and towns north of the city from Afghanistan's Taleban movement.
At least some of the seven rockets heard hit the sprawling airport, sending plumes of smoke and dust from the direction of a military airstrip to the west of the airport.
Several military aircraft, including helicopter gunships and MiG fighters, evacuated the area, some flying to the other end of the airport and some leaving for other bases.
Two civilian aircraft belonging to Afghan Ariana airlines left the airstrip immediately after the barrage began at about 12.00 p.m. (0830 GMT).
There were no immediate reports of casualties and the airport remained tense but free of panic.
Masood's forces have pushed Taleban forces back to within 20 km (12 miles) north of the capital, held by the purist Islamic movement since September 27.
Reporters with Masood's advance force said it pushed a few km (miles) south on Sunday morning to the town of Hussein Kot on the main road running from Kabul to the north.
